Egypt calls for Yemen talks as parliament weighs military support to Saudi Arabia

Egypt advocates exploring "every opportunity" to resolve the Yemen war diplomatically, its foreign minister said, ahead of a parliamentary vote next week on authorising the armed forces to support Saudi Arabia against the Iran-aligned Houthis.

Any direct involvement of the Egyptian military, one of the region's largest, would raise the stakes in the fighting between the kingdom and the Houthis, an increasingly destabilising front in the spreading US-Israeli war on Iran.

item.title: [www.middleeasteye.net] First Arab-American mayor to endorse Trump becomes adviser to president
item.description:
First Arab-American mayor to endorse Trump becomes adviser to president

Submitted by Yasmine El-Sabawi on Thu, 10/22/2026 - 20:58
Amer Ghalib tells MEE he has made it clear to Trump that there must be a 'limit to hate speech' against Arab and Muslim Americans
Former mayor of Hamtramck, Michigan, Amer Ghalib poses for a photo with President Donald Trump in the Oval Office of the White House, published on 15 September 2026 (Amer/Ameer Ghalib/Facebook)
Off

The former mayor of Hamtramck, Michigan, who became the first Arab and Muslim-American elected official to endorse Donald Trump for the US presidency in 2024, has now accepted a role as his adviser on Arab-American affairs. 

Amer Ghalib announced the news on his Facebook account late Wednesday evening, local time, in Washington, DC.

"I would like to express my sincere gratitude to President Trump for appointing me as his Envoy and Advisor for Arab American Affairs, and for his continued trust and support," Ghalib wrote. 

"While I cannot promise to resolve every challenge facing Arab Americans across the United States, I can promise to be a strong and dedicated voice for Arab American communities in the White House, ensuring that their concerns are heard and their perspectives are represented," he added.

Ghalib is currently senior advisor for strategic partnerships at AmeriCorps, a federal agency that promotes civic engagement among Americans. He took that position after it became clear Republican senators would not support him for the role Trump rewarded him with for his endorsement: US ambassador to Kuwait. The country is a critical US ally with several military bases there. 

Ghalib's outspoken criticism of Israel and other comments on social media from his days as a private citizen emerged as a major obstacle to his Senate confirmation, particularly after being amplified by the staunchly pro-Israel Anti-Defamation League and some right-wing news outlets. 

Middle East Eye reached out to the White House for comment but did not hear back by the time of publication. 

'Direct access whenever I need'

Speaking to MEE from Michigan on Thursday, Ghalib did not define the parameters of his new role, but said it was not a full-time position and that he would "meet the president and White House staff as needed to discuss our concerns".

The president granted me a direct access to him whenever I need and that’s what matters the most," Ghalib said. "This... position never existed in any previous administration." 

A physician-turned-politician in 2021 when he assumed leadership of a historic all-Muslim city council in the Detroit suburb, the Yemeni-born Ghalib shook up the 2024 presidential election with his endorsement of Trump, whose previous tenure at the White House was renowned for the Muslim travel ban and close ties to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, for whom he unilaterally recognised all of Jerusalem as well as the Golan Heights as Israeli territory. 

'Historic decision': Hamtramck becomes first US city to boycott Israel
Read More »

By late October 2024, Arab and Muslim neighbourhoods in Michigan, spurred also by a movement called "Arab Americans for Trump", began flipping from Democratic votes to Republican ones, as anger swelled over Joe Biden's handling of Israel's assault on Gaza.

Trump campaigned on a platform to end all wars, and visited Michigan's Arab-American hub, the city of Dearborn, while his opponent, Democratic candidate Kamala Harris, did not. 

But since then, Trump has only secured a superficial ceasefire in Gaza and has joined Israel in an unpopular war on Iran.

Domestically, the political climate for Arabs and Muslims has been repeatedly described to MEE as worse than the post-9/11 period, as Republicans, including the president himself, ramp up anti-Palestinian, anti-Muslim rhetoric in the face of rising progressive figures like New York City Mayor Zohran Mamdani and Michigan Democratic Senate candidate Abdul El-Sayed.

At his most recent 45-minute meeting with the president, Ghalib told MEE that he "started the discussion... on the immigration issues [and] building bridges with the Arab American communities", in addition to "how to put a limit to hate speech done by some radical groups". 

I found an opportunity to continue having direct access to the president so I can deliver the people’s concerns to him and try to get them addressed," Ghalib told MEE in a text message exchange. 

"It’s going to add more work and more stress to me, but I’m willing to go through it - perhaps I can help and continue to be the voice of our community in the White House."

item.description:
Report: UN to end Gaza entry coordination as Israel arrests returnees

The UN has told Palestinian officials it will stop receiving Palestinians returning from Egypt and coordinating their entry into Gaza from mid-November, citing security risks and repeated Israeli arrests, Drop Site News reported, quoting a senior source.

The Palestinian source, who is involved in negotiations, said the decision followed Israel’s arrest of a Palestinian cancer patient and her daughter on Tuesday, when the Rafah crossing reopened after a roughly 10-day suspension prompted by the detention of another returnee. 

Medical evacuees and their companions account for nearly all Palestinians leaving Gaza through the Rafah crossing.

“The United Nations will ask the parties concerned to provide an alternative entity to assume this responsibility; however, its withdrawal will proceed regardless of whether an alternative is secured,” the source said.

Finding a replacement will be difficult because transporting returnees requires coordination with Israel and travel through dangerous areas within the Yellow and Red Line zones, the source said.

While the UN will continue to facilitate medical evacuations, its decision to stop receiving Palestinians returning to Gaza could affect the entire operation of the crossing, the source said.

item.description:
WHO warns of critical shortages at hospitals in Yemen’s Taiz

Hospitals in Yemen’s Taiz governorate are struggling to treat patients as fuel, oxygen, medicines and medical supplies run critically low, the World Health Organization (WHO) said.

The agency said 42 health facilities in Taiz city alone face acute shortages. Fuel shortages are also disrupting water pumping and sanitation, increasing the risk of cholera and other diseases among hundreds of thousands of displaced people.

WHO called for the “immediate facilitation of safe, sustained and unhindered humanitarian access to Taiz, through all available routes, and urgent funding to replenish critical supplies and sustain essential health services”.

item.description:
UAE announce temporary closure of Umm Al Quwain beaches

The UAE has announced the temporary closure of all beaches and coastal areas in Umm Al Quwain, following an oil spill from a tanker.

In a statement by the the Ministry of Climate Change and Environment, it confirmed the oil spill, and noted odours in Sharjah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain "pose no health risks to residents".

"Teams immediately began containment, cordoning, cleanup and remediation with local and federal authorities to limit environmental impacts," it said in a post on X.

"With relevant authorities, the Ministry has temporarily closed all Umm Al Quwain beaches and coastal areas until technical teams complete assessments and identify safety and marine protection measures."

The ministry urged fishermen and those at sea to follow instructions given by authorities and avoid fishing in affected areas. 

The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment confirms the UAE’s technical monitoring and environmental assessment system detected a tanker oil spill affecting Umm Al Quwain’s beaches. Odors noticed in Sharjah, Ajman and Umm Al Quwain pose no health risks to residents. Teams immediately began containment, cordoning, cleanup and remediation with local and federal authorities to limit environmental impacts. Precautionary coastal surveys, monitoring and assessments continue to gauge impacts and protect the marine environment. With relevant authorities, the Ministry has temporarily closed all Umm Al Quwain beaches and coastal areas until technical teams complete assessments and identify safety and marine protection measures. Fishermen and sea users are urged to follow authorities’ instructions and avoid fishing in affected areas. The Ministry urges reliance on official channels, avoidance of rumors, and pledges updates on developments and measures taken. #MOCCAEUAE #UAE

item.description:
First Arab-American mayor to endorse Trump becomes adviser to president

The former mayor of Hamtramck, Michigan, who became the first Arab and Muslim-American elected official to endorse Donald Trump for the US presidency in 2024, has now accepted a role as his adviser on Arab-American affairs. 

Amer Ghalib announced the news on his Facebook account late Wednesday evening, local time, in Washington, DC.

"I would like to express my sincere gratitude to President Trump for appointing me as his Envoy and Advisor for Arab American Affairs, and for his continued trust and support," Ghalib wrote. 

"While I cannot promise to resolve every challenge facing Arab Americans across the United States, I can promise to be a strong and dedicated voice for Arab American communities in the White House, ensuring that their concerns are heard and their perspectives are represented," he added.

Ghalib is currently senior advisor for strategic partnerships at AmeriCorps, a federal agency that promotes civic engagement among Americans. He took that position after it became clear Republican senators would not support him for the role Trump rewarded him with for his endorsement: US ambassador to Kuwait. The country is a critical US ally with several military bases there. 

Read more: First Arab-American mayor to endorse Trump becomes adviser to president

  • The UAE has announced the temporary closure of all beaches and coastal areas in Umm Al Quwain, following an oil spill from a tanker. The Ministry of Climate Change and Environment urged fishermen and those at sea to follow instructions given by authorities and avoid fishing in affected areas.

  • US president Donald Trump suggested that Washington may launch more attacks targeting Iran. "This should have been done a long time ago by other presidents, the Iran war, and we’ve knocked the hell out of them, and we may do it a little bit further," he told reporters. 

  • Saudi Arabia's civil defence issued early warning alerts in Riyadh and later Najran, before it announced that the danger in the two cities had passed. The Saudi-led coalition said it intercepted and destroyed ballistic missiles launched by Yemen’s Houthis towards Riyadh. 

  • Saudi strikes on a residential home in the Taiz governorate killed and injured five civilians overnight. According to the spokesperson for the Sanaa-based Ministry of Health and Environment, one citizen was killed as a result of the attacks and four other were wounded, some in critical condition.

With less than a week before John Healey’s first budget, the latest barometer from the data company GfK indicated confidence plunged by 11 percentage points in October to -24 amid pressure on consumers from the rising cost of living.

Retail sales in Great Britain fell more steeply than expected last month, the latest negative economic update before the chancellor, John Healey, announces his budget next week.

item.title: [World news | The Guardian] Starlink access for Ukraine limited after Trump’s claims satellite service restored, officials say – Europe live
item.description:
The satellite service was still operating at a cap of 161km/hr, crippling key air defences

A war of words has erupted between the Trump administration, officials in Kyiv and Elon Musk over who is to blame for limiting Ukraine’s access to Space X’s military-grade version of Starlink.

The restrictions to Starshield have rendered many of the drones used by Kyiv to strike behind the frontlines inoperable and hampered air defence systems that stop Russian attacks, according to Ukrainian officials.

The US president said on Thursday that the service was running again at full speed, but a European official speaking to the Associated Press denied the service was fully functioning.

What has Trump said?

Trump initially denied any responsibility for the changes to Starshield, telling reporters last Friday: “I don’t know if it was anybody, but it wasn’t me, and I don’t think it was Elon,” referring to Musk, SpaceX’s CEO.

The president has nothing to do with the decisions that are made by Starlink and Starshield and by Mr Musk. That’s a private company. The president doesn’t run that company and can’t direct that company to do anything.

Any limits on speed or usage are decided by the US military and ultimately POTUS.

So I don’t think this is about Elon. I think it’s fundamentally what is America’s policy in Ukraine and Russia going to be.
